title: Respiratory and Circulatory Systems
seo_title: Primary 5 Science: Respiratory and Circulatory Systems Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 5: Human system (Respiratory and circulatory systems)
standard_text: Identify the organs of the human respiratory system and the circulatory system and their functions, and describe how the two systems work together to take in oxygen and transport it, digested food and water to all parts of the body and remove carbon dioxide. Compare how fish (gills) and plants (tiny openings in leaves) take in and give out gases (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on the respiratory and circulatory systems: lungs, air sacs, heart, blood, pulse rate, fish gills and plant gas exchange. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The lungs take in oxygen; the blood carries it.
key_sub: The heart pumps blood to every part of the body.
body_html:
How to think about it

The respiratory system takes in oxygen; the circulatory system carries it to every part of the body.

  • Air: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs. In the air sacs, oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out.
  • Exhaled air has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide and water vapour than inhaled air.
  • The heart pumps blood through blood vessels. Blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells and carbon dioxide away.
  • Fish use gills; plants exchange gases through tiny openings on the leaves.
Example

Why does the heart beat faster during a race?

Muscles need more oxygen and digested food

The heart pumps more blood

Answer: To supply the muscles.

Example

Which gas is there more of in exhaled air?

Cells release carbon dioxide

It is breathed out

Answer: Carbon dioxide (and water vapour).

Common mistakes

  • Thinking we breathe out only carbon dioxide. Exhaled air still has a lot of oxygen.
  • Thinking fish breathe air with lungs. They use gills to take in oxygen dissolved in water.
  • Thinking the heart cleans the blood. It pumps the blood.
  • Thinking plants take in only carbon dioxide. They take in oxygen for respiration too.

faq.q: How do the respiratory and circulatory systems work together?
faq.a: The lungs take in oxygen, which passes into the blood in the air sacs. The heart pumps the blood to carry the oxygen to all parts of the body. Carbon dioxide is carried back to the lungs and breathed out.

faq.q: What is the difference between inhaled and exhaled air?
faq.a: Exhaled air has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide and water vapour than inhaled air.
Fish take in oxygen dissolved in water through their gills.

items.q: Where does oxygen pass into the blood?
c: in the air sacs of the lungs
items.e: The air sacs have very thin walls.

items.q: Compared with the air we breathe in, the air we breathe out has ___ water vapour.
items.e: Exhaled air has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide and water vapour.

items.q: Which part pumps blood around the body?
items.e: The heart pumps blood around the body.

items.q: Air we breathe in passes through the lungs. Where does it go next?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: Which gas does the body need from the air?
items.e: Cells use oxygen to release energy from food.

items.q: Which gas does the body get rid of when we breathe out?
items.e: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas.

items.q: Air reaches the lungs. Where did it come from just before?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: What are the three main parts of the circulatory system?
c: the heart, blood vessels and blood
items.e: Blood flows through blood vessels.

items.q: Compared with the air we breathe in, the air we breathe out has ___ carbon dioxide.
items.e: Exhaled air has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide and water vapour.

items.q: What is the function of the air sacs?
c: Carry blood to and from all parts of the body.
Are where oxygen passes into the blood.
Carries air from the nose to the lungs.
items.e: The air sacs are where oxygen passes into the blood.

items.q: What is the function of the respiratory system?
c: to take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
items.e: Breathing brings air into the lungs.

items.q: What is the function of the gills?
c: Carries air from the nose to the lungs.
Carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells.
Take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.
Take in oxygen dissolved in water for fish.
items.e: The gills take in oxygen dissolved in water for fish.

items.q: What is the function of the circulatory system?
c: to transport substances such as oxygen and digested food around the body
items.e: The heart pumps blood through blood vessels.

items.q: Air we breathe in passes through the nose. Where does it go next?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: What is the pulse?
c: the beat felt at the wrist or neck when the heart pumps blood
items.e: Each pulse beat matches one heartbeat.

items.q: What is the function of the heart?
c: Carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells.
Carry blood to and from all parts of the body.
Let gases enter and leave a plant.
items.e: The heart pumps blood around the body.

items.q: Why does exhaled air make a cold mirror misty?
c: It contains water vapour that condenses on the mirror.
It is colder than the mirror.
items.e: We breathe out water vapour.

items.q: What is the function of the windpipe?
c: Carries air from the nose to the lungs.
Take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.
Let gases enter and leave a plant.
Carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells.
items.e: The windpipe carries air from the nose to the lungs.

items.q: Compared with the air we breathe in, the air we breathe out has ___ oxygen.
items.e: Exhaled air has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide and water vapour.

items.q: Air reaches the windpipe. Where did it come from just before?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: Why does the heart beat faster during exercise?
c: to pump more blood carrying oxygen and digested food to the muscles
items.e: Active muscles need more oxygen.

items.q: Which substance does the blood carry from the lungs to all parts of the body?
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells, and carbon dioxide to the lungs.

items.q: The blood carries digested food. In which direction?
c: from the intestines to all parts of the body
from the small intestine to all parts of the body
from the lungs to all parts of the body
from all parts of the body to the lungs
items.e: The blood transports substances around the body.

items.q: Which substance does the blood carry from the intestines to all parts of the body?
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells, and carbon dioxide to the lungs.

items.q: How do fish take in oxygen?
c: Their gills take in oxygen dissolved in the water.
They take in oxygen through their scales.
items.e: Water flows over the gills.

items.q: Which organ is NOT part of the respiratory system?
items.e: The heart is part of the circulatory system.

items.q: Which part carries air from the nose to the lungs?
items.e: The windpipe carries air from the nose to the lungs.

items.q: The blood carries carbon dioxide. In which direction?
c: from all parts of the body to the lungs
from the small intestine to all parts of the body
from the intestines to all parts of the body
from the lungs to all parts of the body
items.e: The blood transports substances around the body.

items.q: How do the respiratory and circulatory systems work together?
c: The lungs take in oxygen and the blood carries it to all parts of the body.
items.e: The systems depend on each other.

items.q: The blood carries water. In which direction?
c: from the intestines to all parts of the body
from the small intestine to all parts of the body
from the lungs to all parts of the body
from all parts of the body to the lungs
items.e: The blood transports substances around the body.

items.e: The blood transports substances around the body.

items.q: Which gases do plants take in?
c: oxygen (for respiration) and carbon dioxide (in light, to make food)
items.e: Plants respire all the time.

items.q: Why does a fish die when it is taken out of water for a long time?
c: Its gills cannot take in oxygen from the air.
Its scales dry up and turn into lungs.
items.e: Gills work in water.

items.q: Which part lets gases enter and leave a plant?
items.e: The tiny openings on leaves let gases enter and leave a plant.

items.q: What is the function of the blood?
c: Carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells.
Let gases enter and leave a plant.
Carries air from the nose to the lungs.
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells.

items.q: Arjun counts 33 pulse beats in 20 seconds. What is Arjun's pulse rate?
items.e: There are 3 lots of 20 seconds in a minute: 33 × 3 = 99.

c: in all the cells of the body
items.e: Cells release energy from food and make carbon dioxide.

items.e: There are 2 lots of 30 seconds in a minute: 57 × 2 = 114.

items.q: Which substance does the blood carry from all parts of the body to the lungs?
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells, and carbon dioxide to the lungs.

items.q: Why does the body need oxygen?

items.e: Cells use oxygen and food to release energy.

items.q: Aisha counts 17 pulse beats in 10 seconds. What is Aisha's pulse rate?
items.e: There are 6 lots of 10 seconds in a minute: 17 × 6 = 102.

items.q: Imran counts 46 pulse beats in 20 seconds. What is Imran's pulse rate?
items.e: There are 3 lots of 20 seconds in a minute: 46 × 3 = 138.

items.q: Which part takes in oxygen dissolved in water for fish?
items.e: The gills take in oxygen dissolved in water for fish.

items.q: Which waste gas does blood carry to the lungs?
items.e: We breathe it out.

items.q: Which of these is carried by the blood?
items.e: Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

items.q: Hafiz counts 31 pulse beats in 30 seconds. What is Hafiz's pulse rate?
items.e: There are 2 lots of 30 seconds in a minute: 31 × 2 = 62.

items.q: What protects the lungs and heart?
items.e: The ribs form a cage around them.

items.q: Rachel counts 55 pulse beats in 20 seconds. What is Rachel's pulse rate?
items.e: There are 3 lots of 20 seconds in a minute: 55 × 3 = 165.

items.q: Which statement about the heart is correct?
c: It takes in oxygen from the air.
It is a muscular organ that pumps blood all the time.
It is part of the respiratory system.
items.e: The heart never rests.

items.q: Where is the heart found?
c: in the chest, between the lungs
items.e: The ribs protect the heart and lungs.

items.q: When we breathe in, what happens to our chest?
c: It moves up and out as the lungs fill with air.
items.e: The lungs expand.

items.q: Why should we breathe through the nose rather than the mouth?
c: Hairs and mucus in the nose trap dust and germs.
items.e: The air is also warmed and moistened.

items.q: How does regular exercise help the heart?
items.e: A strong heart pumps more blood with each beat.

items.q: Why do fit people often have a lower resting pulse?
c: Their heart is stronger and pumps more blood with each beat.
items.e: Exercise strengthens the heart.

items.q: How do the tiny openings on leaves help a plant at night?
c: They are closed so no gases move.
They let in oxygen for respiration and let out carbon dioxide.
They let in carbon dioxide to make food.
items.e: Plants respire all the time.

items.q: Why is smoking harmful to the lungs?
c: Smoke damages the air sacs, so less oxygen can pass into the blood.
items.e: Smokers often get out of breath easily.

items.q: Why should you measure your pulse three times and find the mean?
c: to make the result more reliable
to make the heart beat faster
because one reading is always wrong
items.e: Repeats reduce the effect of mistakes.

items.q: Limewater turns chalky with carbon dioxide. Which turns limewater chalky faster: inhaled air or exhaled air?
